symptoms: Rosette flowers (petals tied together with silken threads) during early flowering.
Immature bolls showing small entry holes sealed with frass.
Discolored, stained lint and damaged seeds inside bolls.
cultural_controls: Avoid growing susceptible off-season host crops and maintain strict crop termination by December.
Manually collect and burn rosette flowers and fallen early bolls.
Deep summer plowing after harvest to expose overwintering pupae to sunlight and predators.
biological_controls: Release Trichogramma bacterae egg parasitoids @ 60,000 to 1,000,000 per hectare weekly during peak egg-laying.
Apply 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Neem oil (10,000 ppm) as a bio-repellent.
chemical_control_guidance: Consult your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or district agricultural extension officer for government-approved insecticides registered under CIBRC.
Avoid indiscriminate use of synthetic pyrethroids to prevent pest resistance and secondary pest resurgence.
Adhere strictly to recommended pre-harvest safety intervals (PHI).
monitoring_recommendations: Install Pheromone traps @ 5 traps per hectare from 45 days after sowing.
Inspect 20 green bolls per acre weekly; initiate control actions if trap counts exceed 8 male moths per night for 3 consecutive days.

symptoms: Upward or downward curling of leaf margins.
Thickening of leaf veins and enation (leaf-like outgrowths) on the underside of leaves.
Stunted plant growth and severe reduction in boll formation.
cultural_controls: Sow virus-tolerant hybrids recommended for your specific agricultural zone.
Remove and destroy alternative weed hosts (e.g., Abutilon indicum) near field borders.
Maintain balanced Nitrogen fertilization to avoid lush foliage that attracts vector insects.
biological_controls: Conserve natural predators such as ladybird beetles, lacewings, and predatory mites.
Foliar spray of entomopathogenic fungi (Verticillium lecanii) during humid weather.
chemical_control_guidance: Manage the whitefly vector using state-approved selective insect growth regulators.
Consult local agricultural extension officers for registered systemic vector control products.
Never apply broad-spectrum chemicals that destroy beneficial predator populations.
monitoring_recommendations: Install Yellow Sticky Traps @ 10-12 traps per hectare to monitor whitefly vector populations.
Inspect 50 random leaves per field for whitefly nymphs and adults.

symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings (target board pattern) on older leaves.
Yellowing of leaf tissue surrounding the spots leading to premature defoliation.
Sunken, dark lesions on stems and fruit calyx.
cultural_controls: Prune lower leaves up to 30 cm from the ground to improve air circulation.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; use drip irrigation to keep foliage dry.
Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (e.g., maize, legumes).
biological_controls: Foliar application of Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L of water.
Apply sour buttermilk / fermented whey solution (1 L in 10 L water) at early onset.
chemical_control_guidance: Consult your local agricultural extension office for CIBRC-approved protective or systemic fungicides.
Rotate between different fungicide mode-of-action groups to prevent fungal resistance.
Ensure uniform coverage of both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
monitoring_recommendations: Inspect lower canopy foliage twice weekly during periods of warm, humid weather (temp 24-29°C, humidity > 80%).

symptoms: Tiny white flying insects on the underside of leaves.
Yellowing, leaf curling, and secretion of sticky honeydew fostering black sooty mold growth.
Transmission of Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV).
cultural_controls: Cover seedling nursery beds with 40-mesh insect-proof nylon netting.
Plant border crops like maize or sorghum around tomato fields as physical barriers.
Remove and destroy weeds around field perimeters.
biological_controls: Spray Beauveria bassiana or Lecanicillium lecanii bio-insecticide @ 5 g/L during evening hours.
Release Encarsia formosa parasitic wasps or lacewing larvae if available.
chemical_control_guidance: Consult local agricultural extension officers for approved vector management chemistries.
Alternate systemic vector management products with soft soaps or botanical extracts.
monitoring_recommendations: Place Yellow Sticky Traps @ 15-20 traps per hectare across the canopy height.
Monitor traps weekly; take action when adult counts exceed 5 whiteflies per leaf.

symptoms: Small tan to reddish-brown pustules on the lower surface of mature leaves.
Rapid yellowing of foliage and early leaf drop leading to severe yield loss.
cultural_controls: Plant early-maturing, recommended varieties.
Ensure optimal plant spacing for adequate air circulation in the canopy.
biological_controls: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum or Bacillus subtilis bio-fungicide.
chemical_control_guidance: Consult local agricultural extension officers for approved triazole or strobilurin protective fungicides.
Apply at first sign of disease pustules during flowering or pod-filling stages.
monitoring_recommendations: Inspect lower leaf surfaces weekly starting from flowering stage.

symptoms: Small water-soaked lesions on leaves and seed stalks that turn purple with age.
Yellow halo surrounding purple spots, leading to leaf lodging and reduced bulb size.
cultural_controls: Ensure good drainage and avoid standing water in the field.
Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-allium crops.
biological_controls: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L.
chemical_control_guidance: Consult local agricultural extension office for approved protective copper or contact fungicides.
Add a spreader-sticker (wetting agent) to spray mixture due to waxy onion leaves.
monitoring_recommendations: Monitor fields during high humidity and moderate temperatures (21-30°C).

symptoms: Circular, dark, sunken lesions on mature red or green chilli fruits.
Concentric rings of black acervuli inside fruit spots under humid conditions.
cultural_controls: Use disease-free seed treated with bio-fungicide.
Remove and destroy infected fruits immediately to reduce inoculum.
biological_controls: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed and foliar spray @ 5 g/L.
chemical_control_guidance: Consult local agricultural extension officer for CIBRC-registered fruit rot management options.
monitoring_recommendations: Inspect developing fruit clusters weekly during rainy weather.

symptoms: Translucent 'oil-spot' lesions on the upper leaf surface.
White dense cottony fungal growth on the underside of leaves and young shoots.
cultural_controls: Maintain open canopy architecture via timely shoot positioning and leaf removal.
Ensure proper soil drainage and avoid overhead irrigation.
biological_controls: Spray Trichoderma viride or Bacillus subtilis bio-fungicide.
chemical_control_guidance: Consult National Research Centre for Grapes (NRCG) advisory or local extension officers for approved fungicides and pre-harvest intervals.
monitoring_recommendations: Monitor leaves and berry clusters after rainfall during active shoot growth.

bacterial_blight.disease_or_pest: Pomegranate Bacterial Blight / Telya (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. punicae)
symptoms: Water-soaked dark brown spots on leaves, stems, and fruits.
Cracking of fruit along dark brown oily lesions ('Telya' symptoms).
cultural_controls: Prune infected twigs using sterilized shears (disinfect with 70% alcohol).
Orchard sanitation and destruction of infected leaf litter by burning.
biological_controls: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens bio-agent.
chemical_control_guidance: Consult National Research Centre on Pomegranate (NRCP) or local extension officers for recommended copper-based bactericide schedules.
monitoring_recommendations: Inspect orchards closely after monsoon showers or high humidity events.
